chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Sayyārī, from some of the people of al-ʿAskar, he said:

A report was issued from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام that the one engaged in hunting shortens the prayer so long as he remains on the main road; then if he turns away from the road, he performs it in full; and if he returns to it, he shortens.

So this is a weak report, and its narrator is al-Sayyārī. Abū Jaʿfar Ibn Bābawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Fihrist when he mentioned Kitāb al-Nawādir: he excluded from it what al-Sayyārī narrated, and he said: I do not act upon it, nor do I give fatwa by it, due to its weakness.

That whose ruling is such cannot be used to oppose the reports we have presented earlier. Even if it were conceded, it would be possible that its meaning is that whoever is on the main road not for the purpose of hunting must shorten; then if he turns away from it toward hunting, he must perform in full. If, however, while being on the main road his intent was hunting, then the ruling would not differ regarding the obligation of performing in full upon him if his hunting was for diversion, and shortening if his hunting was in pursuit of sustenance.

key_terms.أَتَمَّ: he performs in full; meaning he does not shorten the salat (prayer)
key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: shortening the prayer; the traveler’s reduced salat (prayer)
key_terms.التَّمَامُ: performing the prayer in full; opposite of shortening
key_terms.السَّيَّارِيُّ: al-Sayyārī; the narrator identified as the cause of weakness
key_terms.الصَّيْدِ: hunting; the activity around which the travel ruling is discussed
key_terms.الْجَادَّةِ: the main road or highway; the route mentioned in the report
key_terms.خَبَرٌ ضَعِيفٌ: a weak report; a narration judged unreliable
key_terms.يَقْصُرُ: he shortens; meaning he performs the shortened traveler’s salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening prayer for a hunter in Shia hadith, and how is the weak report about traveling on the main road understood?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling on the prayer of a hunter while traveling and evaluates a specific report attributed to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. The author judges the report weak due to its narrator, al-Sayyārī, and explains that even if accepted, it can be interpreted in a way consistent with earlier reports distinguishing between hunting for amusement and hunting for sustenance.
